title: Glipizide extended-release: research overview and risks
text: Glipizide extended-release is labeled for improving glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes alongside diet and exercise. It can cause severe hypoglycemia. Reported common adverse reactions include dizziness, diarrhea, nervousness, tremor, hypoglycemia and flatulence. The label states that conclusive macrovascular risk reduction has not been established.

title: Glipizide extended-release: reported interactions
text: Concomitant oral miconazole and glipizide can cause severe hypoglycemia. Fluconazole increases glipizide plasma concentrations and may lead to hypoglycemia.

title: Amlodipine: indication and reported risks
text: Amlodipine is labeled for hypertension. Edema is its most common reported adverse reaction and is dose-related. Other reported adverse experiences include fatigue, nausea, abdominal pain and somnolence. Symptomatic hypotension is possible, particularly in severe aortic stenosis.

title: Amlodipine: simvastatin interaction
text: Coadministration of amlodipine with simvastatin increases systemic exposure to simvastatin. This is a reported pharmacokinetic interaction in the label.

title: Lisinopril: reported risks and contraindications
text: Lisinopril is labeled for hypertension. Label warnings include angioedema, renal impairment, hypotension and hyperkalemia. Common adverse reactions in hypertension studies include headache, dizziness and cough. Contraindications include hypersensitivity, specified histories of angioedema, and coadministration with aliskiren in patients with diabetes.

title: Lisinopril: lithium and NSAID interactions
text: Lithium toxicity has been reported with concomitant lithium and ACE inhibitors, including lisinopril. NSAIDs with lisinopril may increase renal impairment risk and reduce antihypertensive efficacy.

title: Alendronate: osteoporosis indication and reported risks
text: Alendronate is labeled for osteoporosis treatment in specified populations. Oral alendronate can irritate the upper gastrointestinal tract; esophagitis, esophageal ulcers and erosions have been reported. Severe bone, joint or muscle pain and osteonecrosis of the jaw have also been reported.

title: Alendronate: calcium and antacid interaction
text: Calcium supplements, antacids and oral medicines containing multivalent cations interfere with alendronate absorption when coadministered.

title: Alendronate: labeled contraindications
text: Alendronate contraindications include esophageal abnormalities that delay emptying, inability to stand or sit upright for at least 30 minutes, hypocalcemia and hypersensitivity to product components.
